name: Critical current and n-value versus applied uniaxial axial strain of commercial REBCO tapes soldered to a Ti-6Al-4V U-spring at 77 K, self-field
plain_name: Find how far a superconducting tape can be stretched before it stops carrying current
description: Tapes from several manufacturers are soldered (45 mm) onto a Ti-6Al-4V U-shaped bending spring; at 77 K in self-field the applied compressive/tensile strain is stepped and Ic and n-value are measured from four-probe V-I curves (10 uV/m) to locate the irreversible strain limit (~0.4%), as needed for HTS cable design.
keywords: Find how far a superconducting tape can be stretched before it stops carrying current

sources.citation: Zhou, Yagotintsev, Gao, Haugan, van der Laan, Nijhuis, Critical Current of Various REBCO Tapes Under Uniaxial Strain, IEEE Trans. Appl. Supercond. 26(4) 8401304 (2016), doi:10.1109/TASC.2016.2535202

requirements.rationale: All Ic-strain measurements were made at 77 K.
Ic is measured by four-point transport, requiring current and voltage-tap wiring to the sample.
Optional: the tape is soldered over a 45 mm length of the U-spring.
